definitions.name: \mathcal{H}^{u}_d(L)
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{H}^{u}_d(L)=\left\{g:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb{R}:\max_{|v|\leq m_u}\lVert D^v g\rVert_\infty\leq L,\ \max_{|v|=m_u}\sup_{x\neq x'}\frac{|D^v g(x)-D^v g(x')|}{\lVert x-x'\rVert_2^{u-m_u}}\leq L\right\},\qquad m_u=\lceil u\rceil-1.\]

definitions.name: \mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band}}
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band}}(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L,\varepsilon,f_{-},f_{+},x_0)=\left\{P:\bigwedge_{j\in\mathcal J}\mathrm{ass}_j(P)\right\},\] where \(\mathcal J\) is exactly the member-property list below.

definitions.name: \mathfrak{H}_{G}
definitions.construction: Starting from the localized KBRW \(R\)-normal equations at \(x_0\) and tuning \((h_n^*,k_n^*)\), form the local empirical basis Gram matrix from the same weighted observations that enter the higher-order kernels. Replace the density-based projection by its empirically centered inverse-Gram expansion, apply partition-lattice M\"obius inversion to cancel repeated-index collisions, select the finite truncation order from the localized remainder bound, screen the spectrum, and clip both the score ratio and every exceptional-event fallback to \([-2L,2L]\). The handle forbids a density estimate and uses the \(G_n=1\) inequality as the effective-sample rank condition; the exact kernel algebra is to be derived in \(\mathrm{thm:rank\mbox{-}feasible\mbox{-}local\mbox{-}hoif}\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak{H}_{P}
definitions.construction: Starting from the causal bilinear residual identity in a window of radius \(h_n^*\) about \(x_0\), partition the window at multiple distance resolutions, select bounded close pairs or tuples with explicit empty-cell fallbacks, and choose a finite signed combination whose vanishing moments separately annihilate the lower Taylor terms of \(\pi_P\) and \(\mu_{0,P}\). Fit the remaining local \(R\)-projection at rank \(k_n^*\), clip all normalizations and the final estimate to \([-2L,2L]\), and derive the correction order, scales, weights, collision accounting, and enlarged validity region in \(\mathrm{oeq:multiresolution\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}frontier}\). No candidate order or weight vector is presupposed.

definitions.name: \widehat{\tau}^{*}_n(x_0)
definitions.construction: \[\widehat{\tau}^{*}_n(x_0)=\operatorname{clip}_{[-2L,2L]}\left\{G_n\widehat{\tau}^{G}_n(x_0)+P_n\widehat{\tau}^{P}_n(x_0)\right\}.\] Each branch is everywhere defined by its own bounded fallbacks before this deterministic switch.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band}}\), the continuous versions selected by the H\"older restrictions satisfy \[\tau_P(x_0)=\mu_{1,P}(x_0)-\mu_{0,P}(x_0)=\mathbb{E}_P[Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x_0].\]
statements.justification: The point target must be a version-invariant causal law functional before its risk can be studied.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. work with the same continuous H\"older CATE; this lemma makes the version choice explicit for the positive-band class.
statements.consumer: Every branch risk bound and the final minimax comparison use this identified point target.

statements.statement: For every \(n\geq2\), the minimizer \((h_n^*,k_n^*)\) exists, is unique after lexicographic selection, and satisfies \(G_n+P_n=1\) and \(G_nP_n=0\). Moreover, \(r_n^*\) equals the exact infimum of the three-term KBRW objective over \(\mathcal T_n\).
statements.justification: The deterministic split must cover every sample size without an unanalysed tuning boundary.
statements.gap: KBRW optimize asymptotic choices; the exact lexicographic optimizer and exhaustive branch selector are new bookkeeping required by a single total estimator.
statements.consumer: The unified estimator can switch without data-dependent model selection or uncovered equality cases.

statements.statement: If \(\pi_P\) and \(\mu_{0,P}\) are supplied to the local \(R\)-normal equations and the nuisance-product correction is suppressed, then the oracle local-polynomial branch with \(k=1\) satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band}}}\mathbb{E}_P|\widehat\tau_n^{\mathrm{or}}(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)|\leq C\left\{h^\gamma+(nh^d)^{-1/2}\right\}.\] Optimizing \(h\) gives the classical pointwise-regression rate \(n^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+d)}\); if both outcome regressions are supplied, the direct plug-in equals \(\tau_P(x_0)\) exactly.
statements.justification: This is the required sanity reduction to ordinary random-design pointwise regression.
statements.gap: The new corrections must disappear rather than create a spurious density or Gram penalty when the nuisances are oracle-known.
statements.consumer: Users in randomized trials or oracle nuisance benchmarks recover the familiar local-polynomial rate as a corollary.

statements.statement: For every compact \(K\subset(0,\infty)^3\), there are \(C_K<\infty\) and \(n_K\) such that, for every \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in K\), every \(n\geq n_K\) with \(G_n=1\), and the estimator \(\widehat{\tau}^{G}_n(x_0)\) derived from \(\mathfrak H_G\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band}}}\mathbb{E}_P\left|\widehat{\tau}^{G}_n(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|\leq C_K\left[(h_n^*)^\gamma+\left\{\frac{h_n^*}{(k_n^*)^{1/d}}\right\}^{\alpha+\beta}+\left(\frac{1}{N_n^*}\left\{1+\frac{k_n^*}{N_n^*}\right\}\right)^{1/2}\right]=C_K r_n^*.\] The estimator is an everywhere-defined same-sample M\"obius-stabilized empirical-Gram local HOIF and uses no estimate or smoothness condition for \(f_P\). On the explicitly restricted class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band}}\), the construction therefore attains the KBRW three-term objective on the \(G_n\) branch without the density-estimation or density-ratio condition used in KBRW Theorem 2. No inclusion relation between the two theorem classes is asserted.
statements.justification: It localizes same-sample stabilization at the random effective size \(N_n^*\) and, on the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class, avoids a density-estimation remainder without a logarithmic risk loss.
statements.gap: Liu et al. prove stabilization for global bilinear forms with deterministic sample size, while the KBRW upper theorem uses a local covariate-law condition; neither result supplies density-free control of weighted occupancy, leverage, and collisions in the same local sample under the fixed positive-band restriction.
statements.consumer: It supplies density-free optimal pointwise CATE estimation whenever the optimizer-selected local rank is empirically feasible.

statements.statement: Derive, rather than posit, a finite correction-order map \(q(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d)\), a finite family of distance resolutions, and signed weights for \(\mathfrak H_P\) whose separate propensity and control-regression vanishing moments leave bias at most \((h_n^*/(k_n^*)^{1/d})^{\alpha+\beta}\) and whose Hoeffding components are at most the variance term in \(r_n^*\), uniformly on every compact \(K\subset(0,\infty)^3\) whenever \(P_n=1\). Determine the smallest such order and exhibit a derived nonempty open set \(U\subset(0,\infty)^3\setminus\mathcal R_{\mathrm{bank}}\) with \(U\cap(\{\beta>\alpha\}\cup\{\alpha>1\})\neq\varnothing\) on which the construction works. The scheme must remain total under empty cells and singular empirical local Grams and must not estimate \(f_P\).
statements.justification: The correction order and enlarged asymmetric smoothness frontier are the genuinely open mathematical content of the sparse-local branch.
statements.gap: The banked first-difference identity works only on \(0<\beta<\alpha\leq1\); Dobriban et al. remove polynomial trends for homoskedastic variance, not the two unequally smooth causal nuisances in a local \(R\)-ratio.
statements.consumer: A solution gives an implementable density-free estimator for sparse local windows, including a region with reversed nuisance ordering or propensity smoothness above one.

statements.statement: Let the finite order, resolutions, weights, and nonempty open extension set be those derived in \(\mathrm{oeq:multiresolution\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}frontier}\). For every compact \(K\) in its derived validity region, there are \(C_K<\infty\) and \(n_K\) such that, for every \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in K\), every \(n\geq n_K\) with \(P_n=1\), and the total estimator \(\widehat{\tau}^{P}_n(x_0)\) derived from \(\mathfrak H_P\), \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band}}}\mathbb{E}_P\left|\widehat{\tau}^{P}_n(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|\leq C_K r_n^*.\] Its validity region contains \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{bank}}\) and contains the derived open set \(U\) outside it, so this is a strict region extension of the banked close-pair theorem. The bound has no logarithmic loss and uses no density estimate or density smoothness.
statements.justification: This turns the rank-stressed regime from a logarithmically inflated fallback into an exact-benchmark branch.
statements.gap: Shen et al. and Dobriban et al. analyze variance identities with one regression nuisance; their cancellations do not deliver the causal bilinear target or the required asymmetric H\"older product bias.
statements.consumer: It covers observational studies whose optimizer demands more local nuisance resolution than the empirical window rank permits.

statements.statement: For every compact \(K\) on which the derived rank-stressed construction is valid, there are \(C_K<\infty\) and \(n_K\) such that, for every \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in K\) and \(n\geq n_K\), the single total estimator \(\widehat{\tau}^{*}_n(x_0)\) satisfies \[\sup_{P\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathrm{band}}}\mathbb{E}_P\left|\widehat{\tau}^{*}_n(x_0)-\tau_P(x_0)\right|\leq C_K\inf_{(h,k)\in\mathcal T_n}\left[h^\gamma+\left(\frac{h}{k^{1/d}}\right)^{\alpha+\beta}+\left\{\frac{1}{nh^d}\left(1+\frac{k}{nh^d}\right)\right\}^{1/2}\right]=C_Kr_n^*.\] It switches only through the deterministic exhaustive partition \((G_n,P_n)\), has bounded fallbacks on every sample, and neither estimates the covariate density nor assumes its smoothness. On the explicitly restricted class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{band}}\), it attains the optimizer-defined KBRW mean-absolute-risk benchmark without the density-estimation or density-ratio condition used in KBRW Theorem 2. This is a rate-and-construction comparison on the fixed positive-band class, not an assertion that either theorem class contains the other.
statements.justification: The headline result stitches complementary density-free mechanisms into one benchmark-rate estimator on the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class without a logarithmic transition penalty.
statements.gap: The KBRW upper theorem uses a covariate-law condition, stabilized HOIFs cover only the below-rank global branch, and close-pair variance estimators do not target CATE; no paper supplies this exhaustive local synthesis on the fixed positive-band class, and no class-inclusion comparison is claimed.
statements.consumer: Pointwise treatment-effect analyses can attain the published benchmark under a primitive positive design-density band without choosing or estimating a density model.

sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. observational random design on \([0,1]^d\) with an unknown Lebesgue density satisfying only \(f_{-}\leq f_P\leq f_{+}\).
sampling_model.units: Each unit contributes \(O=(X,A,Y)\) with bounded potential outcomes.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is binary, consistent, and conditionally exchangeable given \(X\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The propensity and control regression may be estimated at their known H\"older indices inside the local \(R\)-construction. The design density is never estimated, and no density smoothness or density-estimation rate is imposed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 bounds pointwise CATE risk at the three-term optimized rate under its stated local covariate-law estimation condition.
Theorem 1 gives same-sample stabilized empirical-HOIF bias, variance \(O(n^{-1}+k n^{-2})\), and a Gaussian limit for global bilinear forms when \(k\lesssim n/(\log n)^3\).
The empirical-HOIF construction replaces density estimation by an inverse sample Gram computed on an independent sample under a below-rank restriction.
Section 2, Theorem 2.1 gives a finite two-scale close-pair upper bound for homoskedastic variance and a separate density-regular HOIF comparison.
The pointwise variance theorem analyzes a local-polynomial pairwise-difference \(U\)-statistic under random design.
The paper establishes doubly robust confidence bands in a first-order local-smoothing regime.

tldr: A single bounded local \(R\)-estimator is to attain the KBRW pointwise-CATE benchmark on an explicitly restricted fixed positive two-sided covariate-density-band class. On \(G_n\), a same-sample M\"obius-stabilized empirical local Gram removes density estimation; on \(P_n\), a finite-order signed multiresolution close-pair correction handles rank stress. The correction order and asymmetric validity frontier are derived objects, with a required nonempty open extension beyond the banked \(0<\beta<\alpha\leq1\) wedge. Within this fixed-band class, the estimator avoids the density-estimation or density-ratio condition used by the KBRW upper theorem at the same objective; no weakening, tightening, or inclusion relation between theorem classes is claimed.

project_justification.gap: KBRW publish the sharp pointwise-CATE benchmark and an upper theorem with a local covariate-law condition. It is unresolved whether that same three-term objective is attainable without density estimation or a density-ratio condition after explicitly restricting attention to laws with a fixed positive two-sided density band. Existing density-free empirical HOIF results are global and rank-limited, while close-pair results target noncausal variance functionals.
project_justification.niche: The explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class supplies local mass but no smooth density model. Within that class, the optimizer reveals two complementary obstacles: same-sample inverse-Gram dependence below local rank and sparse collision geometry above it. This restriction is not asserted to weaken, tighten, or contain the KBRW theorem class.
project_justification.fill: On the fixed positive-band class, the project derives both branch constructions, proves the KBRW three-term risk envelope without density estimation, a density-ratio condition, or logarithmic loss, extends the close-pair smoothness region, and combines the branches through the deterministic exhaustive selector \((G_n,P_n)\) with bounded fallbacks.

related_work: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024) define the destination benchmark and local higher-order \(R\)-learner, and their upper theorem uses a local covariate-law estimation condition. The present result uses their objective as a benchmark and, on the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class, seeks attainment without density estimation or a density-ratio condition; it makes no weakening, tightening, or inclusion claim about the two theorem classes. Liu, Li, Gu, and Liu (2026) provide the M\"obius, Neumann-remainder, and graph-counting method adapted on the rank-feasible branch, but their target is a global bilinear form. Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2017) establish the independent empirical-Gram ancestor. Dobriban, Mukherjee, Robins, and Wang (2026, Section 2, Theorem 2.1) motivate the two-regime synthesis and projected-pair screening for homoskedastic variance. Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020) supply the closest pairwise-difference \(U\)-statistic analysis. Robins et al. (2008, 2017) inform finite higher-order correction, without delivering the localized causal residual algebra. Lee, Okui, and Whang (2017) concern first-order CATE inference and are not a theorem-level target here.
technical_internal_limitation: The rank-stressed theorem rests on solving the open moment-cancellation and Hoeffding-accounting problem in \(\mathrm{oeq:multiresolution\mbox{-}order\mbox{-}frontier}\). A singular local empirical Gram only triggers a bounded estimator fallback; it is not evidence for an all-estimator lower bound. The KBRW support-hole fuzzy-hypothesis construction is outside the fixed-positive-band class and is not used for a converse.
honest_scope: Identification and the oracle local-regression reduction are standard. The new theorem-level work is the two upper-bound branches and their exact deterministic stitching. The finite multiresolution order, signed weights, and maximal smoothness region are deliberately left for derivation rather than assumed. No density-induced slowdown, new minimax lower bound, adaptive unknown-smoothness guarantee, or elbow-uniform confidence interval is claimed.
seeds: Unified density-free attainment of the KBRW objective on the fixed positive-band class by a deterministic stabilized-HOIF and multiresolution close-pair switch.
Localized same-sample M\"obius empirical-Gram HOIF under random window occupancy.
A semiparametric efficiency characterization in the regression-like branch.
Policy regret induced by optimizer-rate pointwise CATE estimation.
Conformal inversion for a pointwise conditional causal effect.
Adaptation to unknown \((\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\) without density estimation.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction; Theorem 1; Section 4.1, especially the local \(R\)-projection and quadratic correction; Theorem 2; and the Discussion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: KBRW's third-order remainder contains an estimated local covariate law. On the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class, the first changed proof step is to replace that projection by a same-sample empirical local Gram on \(G_n\) and by signed close-pair geometry on \(P_n\). Searches for the exact pointwise-CATE and two-method pair returned no closer construction.
seed_details.exact_pair_occupied: No located theorem treats pointwise CATE with both a same-sample local empirical Gram and a rank-stressed causal close-pair branch under only a fixed density band.
seed_details.closest_subsumption_check: KBRW supply the target objective under their own upper-theorem conditions; the fixed positive-band result seeks density-free attainment without asserting inclusion between theorem classes. Liu et al. and Dobriban et al. each supply only one nonlocal or noncausal component.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The focal object is the total estimator and its exact optimizer risk on the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class, not a generic application of HOIF machinery; Theorem 3 states the KBRW relation only as a benchmark-and-construction comparison.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: this is immediate from KBRW because their Theorem 2 already attains the rate. Response: the present theorem is posed on the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class and must attain the same objective with no density estimate or density-ratio condition through two new rank-regime constructions. It does not claim that this class weakens, tightens, or contains the KBRW theorem class.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction and contribution summary; Theorem 1; the M\"obius decomposition lemma; proof sketch; and Concluding Remarks.
seed_details.proof_boundary: Liu et al. use a global deterministic sample size and a bilinear target. The first changed step is their M\"obius collision expansion after replacing \(n\) by random weighted local occupancy \(N_n^*\), with bandwidth-dependent leverage and a local \(R\)-ratio. Searches found no local pointwise-CATE theorem for this target--method pair.
seed_details.exact_pair_occupied: No search result localizes the same-sample M\"obius theorem to a bandwidth-dependent pointwise causal \(R\)-ratio.
seed_details.closest_subsumption_check: Liu et al. supply the global combinatorics, while KBRW supply the local causal decomposition; neither source controls their interaction.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: This is a rate theorem for a named localized estimator, so M11 is the native shape rather than a bare estimation rung.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: localizing Theorem 1 is a routine effective-sample-size substitution. Rebuttal: the same observations determine occupancy, Gram inversion, residual kernels, and the ratio denominator, so global exchangeability and leverage counts do not survive by substitution.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Introduction; model and Section 2, Theorem 2.1; low-regularity estimator; projected close-pair bias and availability lemmas; and Discussion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The donor cancels one regression trend for constant variance. The first changed step is its conditional pair identity: the CATE kernel needs separate vanishing moments for propensity and control-regression increments while preserving a positive local \(R\)-Gram. Searches against Shen et al. and HOIF papers found no causal version.
seed_details.exact_pair_occupied: Searches found pairwise variance estimators and causal HOIF estimators separately, but no signed multiresolution causal residual kernel with asymmetric nuisance cancellation.
seed_details.closest_subsumption_check: Dobriban et al. do not have treatment residuals or a local CATE ratio, and Shen et al. have only one unknown regression trend.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The nonempty open extension and derived correction order prevent a single-witness or routine first-difference restatement.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: higher-order differencing automatically extends the banked wedge. Rebuttal: unequal nuisance smoothness creates asymmetric cross terms and ratio bias; the correction order and feasible open region must emerge jointly with the Hoeffding variance calculation.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Theorem 2 and the Discussion paragraph that explicitly leaves the estimator distribution and inference open.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step is to replace a risk decomposition by a regime-uniform H\'{a}jek--Hoeffding projection with feasible variance estimation; searches located first-order CATE bands and local-polynomial coverage theory but no degenerate-HOIF or close-pair result.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposed limit law would be the headline object, but its prerequisite estimator is not yet available on both branches.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: Liu et al.'s Gaussian limit and Calonico et al.'s studentization can simply be combined. Rebuttal: at the elbow the first-order projection may vanish and the local random-coefficient degenerate component can be first order.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Theorem 1, its central-limit discussion, and the counterfactual-mean example in the setup.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The destination search was pointwise CATE plus semiparametric efficiency. The first changed step would be a local asymptotic experiment for a bandwidth-dependent point target.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The efficiency lane was generated as required, but the point-evaluation target is irregular and does not support a nontrivial fixed-model bound.

seed_details.anchor_opened: Theorem 1; its localized fuzzy-hypothesis construction; the density remark following the theorem; and the Discussion.
seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step would be a testing family whose density remains above \(f_{-}\), because KBRW's support-hole construction cannot certify a positive-band converse.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: A valid converse would need a positive-band region of laws; a support-hole witness or local-Gram failure cannot serve as the information bound.

seed_details.proof_boundary: The first changed step would replace known \((h_n^*,k_n^*)\) by a two-dimensional Lepski selector while preserving the local Gram and pair exceptional-event bounds.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The adaptation problem is mathematically credible but violates the version's known-smoothness design decision.
seed_details.red_team: Cynical objection: the topic fixes all smoothness inputs as known, so adaptation changes the problem and risks an unavoidable logarithmic price. The objection is decisive for this version.

literature_map: Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Theorems 1--2 and Section 4.1) supply the pointwise-CATE benchmark, local \(R\)-projection, and localized quadratic-HOIF decomposition; their upper theorem uses a local covariate-law estimation condition. The present comparison is limited to attaining the same objective without density estimation or a density-ratio condition on the explicitly restricted fixed positive-band class, with no claimed class inclusion. Liu, Li, Gu, and Liu (2026, Theorem 1 and the M\"obius lemma) remove sample splitting and stabilize an empirical inverse Gram for global bilinear forms under \(k\lesssim n/(\log n)^3\), but do not localize at random effective size \(nh^d\). Liu, Mukherjee, Newey, and Robins (2017) are the independent-Gram density-free ancestor. Dobriban, Mukherjee, Robins, and Wang (2026, Section 2, Theorem 2.1, and the projected-pair lemmas) join close-pair and HOIF regimes for homoskedastic variance, while Shen, Gao, Witten, and Han (2020) supply the local pairwise-difference and Hoeffding precedent. Robins et al. (2008, 2017) supply finite-order higher-order bias--variance accounting. Searches through September 11, 2026 found no paper combining same-sample local stabilization and multiresolution causal close pairs for pointwise CATE on this fixed positive-band class, and no closer result subsumes the proposed kernel.

novelty_justification: The closest published theorem is KBRW Theorem 2, which attains the three-term pointwise-CATE benchmark under its stated local covariate-law estimation condition. The proposed headline instead fixes the explicitly restricted positive two-sided density-band class and asks for the identical optimizer-defined objective using no density estimate or density-ratio condition. This is a density-free attainment claim within that restricted class, not a strict assumption weakening, strict tightening, or class-inclusion comparison with KBRW. The second closest result is Liu et al. (2026), whose same-sample M\"obius theorem is global and below-rank; localization makes occupancy, leverage, Gram coefficients, and HOIF kernels dependent. The rank-stressed branch is not a relabeling of Dobriban et al. (2026, Section 2, Theorem 2.1): its first identity is a causal bilinear \(R\)-equation with two unequally smooth nuisances, and its theorem must derive a finite cancellation order and a nonempty open region beyond \(0<\beta<\alpha\leq1\).
